mechanistic_decomposition.modification_failure_mechanism: Across both evaluators, R1 and R3 reach 60-80% M-all-pass rates (passing G_mod_c for those reconstructions). R2 only reaches 30% M-all-pass (5 of 10 Arm M candidates are the trigger-FAIL deferrals both evaluators classified as DIFFERENT with M1-M4=0). R2's 30% < 70% threshold is the single sub-failure that drives G_mod_c FALSE for both evaluators. G_mod_a (mean 3.07 < 3.5), G_mod_b (56.7% < 80%), and G_mod_d (6.7-10pp << 50pp threshold) are all consequences of the same underlying pattern: when M is genuinely expressed, the modification works; the failure mode is concentrated in the 5 R2_B M-deferrals where the model produced no report.
mechanistic_decomposition.preservation_failure_mechanism: The Manhattan-distance preservation gates (G_pres_a, G_pres_b) are inflated entirely by the same 5 R2_B M-deferrals: 5 records with total_score=0 (A) or 1/0/1/0 (B) drive within-recon Manhattan to 15.6 (A) and 14.0 (B), compared to 0.33-0.48 for Arm C. C12 axes are preserved (no axis BROKEN under the 30%/30pp rule); §11.4 inter-evaluator agreement is high (93.3% identity exact agreement, MAE ≤ 0.23). The preservation failure is a CONSEQUENCE of the modification failure (the 5 records where the model didn't produce a report) rather than a separate identity-erosion mechanism.
mechanistic_decomposition.the_two_failures_are_mechanistically_one: Both Modification Success and Non-target Identity Preservation fail because of the same 5 records (B0014, B0017, B0018, B0034, B0045 in R2_B Arm M, the trigger-FAIL deferrals both evaluators classified as DIFFERENT). Without these 5 records: G_mod_b would be 17/25 = 68% (still FAIL but closer); G_mod_c R2 would be 3/5 = 60% (still FAIL); G_pres_a/b would drop substantially because Manhattan distance is dominated by the zero-scored records; C12 axes would drop to ~0% (5 fewer zero-axis records out of 30). The protocol's frozen gates do not carve out per-record exceptions; the literal application of §14 gives MODIFICATION_AND_PRESERVATION_FAILURE.

what_this_does_not_claim: The experiment does not claim that intent-driven modification is impossible. The 2 of 3 reconstructions (R1, R3) where the model produced a report show the modification works at the candidate level. The failure is concentrated in R2's 5 trigger-FAIL deferrals.

The experiment does not claim that BIB 4-dim identity is generally eroded. C12 axes are preserved, inter-evaluator agreement is high, and Arm C is within the envelope on all 6 per-(R,B) cells for both evaluators.
The experiment does not claim that Claude-Opus-4-7 cannot produce the modification. Evaluator B's R3 achieved 80% M-all-pass; R1 and R3 show the modification works when the model produces a report.
